t: That part of title III of the Act of February 18, 1946 (60 Stat. 20; 37 U. S. C. 112c), which authorizes transportation of dependents and household effects of civilian and naval personnel of the Naval Establishment stationed outside continental United States is amended by deleting therefrom all reference to Naval personnel.

fable.w: This section is a technical amendment that removes references to Naval personnel from an earlier provision on transporting dependents and household effects. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. There is no real tempting reading here; the only people mentioned are federal personnel affected by a benefit provision, not participants in a federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by deleting therefrom all reference to Naval personnel

qwen_block.w: This section is a legislative amendment that removes a specific class of personnel (Naval personnel) from a statute authorizing transportation benefits. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a change in statutory eligibility criteria.
qwen_block.s: That part of title III of the Act of February 18, 1946 (60 Stat. 20; 37 U. S. C. 112c), which authorizes transportation of dependents and household effects of civilian and naval personnel of the Naval Establishment stationed outside continental United States is amended by deleting therefrom all reference to Naval personnel.

opus.w: This section only deletes references to Naval personnel from an existing law that authorizes transporting dependents and household effects. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. Mentioning personnel or the Naval Establishment does not create any consultation, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The words "Naval Establishment" and "civilian and naval personnel" might make this look like it touches on government decisions involving people. But that reading fails. The section only amends an existing law about transporting dependents and household goods. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue that would involve anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment that modifies the eligibility for a specific benefit (transportation of dependents) by removing naval personnel from the scope. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. It is not an application process, nor does it involve public hearings, advisory committees with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes. The definition of participation requires interaction with people outside the government before a decision is made; this text merely changes the statutory text defining who receives a benefit.
qwen_chat.s: That part of title III of the Act of February 18, 1946 (60 Stat. 20; 37 U. S. C. 112c), which authorizes transportation of dependents and household effects of civilian and naval personnel of the Naval Establishment stationed outside continental United States is amended by deleting therefrom all reference to Naval personnel.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that deleting references to naval personnel affects the rights or participation of those personnel, or that the amendment process itself involves participation. However, the text is purely a legislative amendment instruction regarding the scope of a benefit statute. It does not establish a process for outsiders to consult with the government, nor does it grant rights to sue or comment. It simply changes the eligibility criteria for a benefit (transportation of dependents).
